Children must be 3 years old on or before September 1 to register for K0, 4 years old for K1, and 5 years old for K2. See a full list for all grades here: https://www.bostonpublicschools.org/enrollment/welcome-services/registration

To register your child, you must provide: 1) Child’s original birth certificate, I-94 form, or passport (use of passport requires completion of BPS Parent Affidavit), 2) Child’s up-to-date immunization record, 3) Child's up-to-date physical exam record (within the last year), 4) Parent/Guardian’s photo identification, 5) Two proofs of Boston residency from the list provided here: https://www.bostonpublicschools.org/enrollment/welcome-services/registration

BPS uses a Home-Based student assignment policy for kindergarten through grade 8. Families receive a customized list of school choices based on their home address, including schools within a one-mile radius and nearby high-quality schools. Learn more here: https://www.bostonpublicschools.org/enrollment/welcome-services/student-assignment-policy

If you're missing some required documents, please contact a BPS Welcome Center to discuss your situation. They can guide you on alternative documentation or next steps. For contact information, visit: https://www.bostonpublicschools.org/enrollment/welcome-services/welcome-centers-locations

Seats for K1 are limited and not guaranteed. While BPS offers over 2,400 K1 seats and is working to expand, not every school has a K1 classroom. Assignments are based on availability and other factors. For more details, please refer to our registration FAQs: https://www.bostonpublicschools.org/enrollment/welcome-services/faq

Visit a BPS Welcome Center with your photo ID and two proofs of Boston residency. Changing your address may affect your school and transportation options. More information: https://www.bostonpublicschools.org/enrollment/welcome-services/change-of-address

Accepted documents include: a utility bill (not water or cell phone) dated within the past 60 days; a deed or mortgage payment dated within the past 60 days, or a property tax bill dated within the last year; a W2 form dated within the year, or a payroll stub dated within the past 60 days; a bank or credit card statement dated within the past 60 days; a letter from an approved government agency dated within the past 60 days; a current lease, Section 8 Agreement, or BPS Landlord Affidavit dated within a year. Note: The two proofs cannot be from the same category.

If your child's current school is within your new home-based assignment area, they can remain at their current school and may still be eligible for transportation. If the school is not within the new home-based area, your child can remain but will not be eligible for transportation, or you can select a new school within your choice list where they may be eligible for transportation.
No, BPS cannot change your child's bus stop until you officially update your address at a Welcome Center.
The BPS Landlord Affidavit form is available on the BPS website in multiple languages. Access it at: https://www.bostonpublicschools.org/enrollment/welcome-services/change-of-address

To update your address, visit a BPS Welcome Center with your photo ID and two proofs of Boston residency. Accepted documents must be from different categories and dated within the specified time frames.

Failing to update your address may result in miscommunication regarding school assignments and transportation. It's essential to keep your address current to ensure your child receives appropriate services.
Yes, BPS does not accept water or cell phone bills as proof of residency. Ensure you provide two accepted documents from different categories.
Yes, a letter from an approved government agency dated within the past 60 days is accepted. Approved agencies include the DOR, DCF, DTA, DYS, or Social Security.
Yes, a current lease, Section 8 Agreement, or BPS Landlord Affidavit dated within a year is accepted as one of the two required proofs of residency.
You can explore your family's new list of school choices by entering your new address at DiscoverBPS.org.
If you have questions, contact a BPS Welcome Center for assistance. They can guide you through the process and answer any concerns you may have.
Currently, BPS requires families to visit a Welcome Center in person to update their address. Ensure you bring the necessary documents.
If you don't have two proofs of residency, contact a BPS Welcome Center. They can advise on alternative documentation or next steps.
Updating your address ensures that your child receives accurate school assignments and transportation services. Delays may result in missed communications or ineligibility for certain services.

Children must be 3 years old on or before September 1 to register for K0, 4 years old for K1, and 5 years old for K2. For more details, visit https://www.bostonpublicschools.org/enrollment/welcome-services/registration.
K2 is a full-day, six-hour program for 5-year-olds, offered in all BPS elementary schools and early learning centers.
Yes, all children who apply for K2 are guaranteed a school assignment, though a specific school assignment cannot be guaranteed due to space limitations.
It is recommended to register during Round One (January) for the best chance at securing a spot in your preferred school.
Round One registration takes place in January and gives families the best chance at securing a spot in their chosen school, especially with limited open seats.
While assignment is guaranteed, due to space constraints, a specific school assignment may not be possible. Be sure to inquire about open seats during School Choice season.
Inquire about the number of available seats during School Choice season to get updated information for your preferred school.
Countdown to Kindergarten is a program offering free parent-child playgroups, readiness tips, and workshops to support families in transitioning to Kindergarten.
Visit www.countdowntokindergarten.org for resources, publications, and upcoming events, or call 617-635-9288.
The Great Starts tool helps families find early childhood programs for 3- and 4-year-olds in Boston. While BPS offers Pre-K programming, school assignment is not guaranteed.
A child must be 5 years old on or before September 1 to enroll in Kindergarten (K2) for that school year.
State law requires that children must attend school starting in the September of the calendar year they turn six years old.
Yes, all Kindergarten students are guaranteed a seat in their assigned school through the highest grade offered, but specific school assignments may be subject to space availability.
You can learn about the BPS registration process and important dates by visiting www.bostonpublicschools.org/register.
BPS offers a range of events, including information sessions and school previews, to help families find the best school fit and understand the registration process.
Yes, virtual information sessions for the 2025-2026 school year have been recorded. You can view the recordings for the Dec 5 morning and evening sessions on the BPS website.

School previews are held between November and January. These events allow families to tour schools, meet leaders and staff, and learn about various programs. More information is available on the BPS website.
You can fill out the School Preview Times Interest Form to select the schools you're interested in. The schools will then reach out to you with more details.
Yes, you can select up to 5 schools on the form. If you are interested in attending sessions at more than 5 schools, you can complete the form multiple times.
You can email welcomeservices@bostonpublicschools.org for any questions related to registration.
To submit a transfer, a parent must visit a BPS Welcome Center with a photo ID. Transfers are for students moving from one Boston Public School to another.
The transfer period ends on November 30, 2024, for students in grades 1-12, and on January 31, 2025, for students in grades K0-K2.
Due to limited seat availability, transfers are not guaranteed. If available, students will be assigned to their top-ranked school with an available seat.
If a transfer does not go through, the student will be placed on the waitlist for their requested school.

Prior to August 1, students can be placed on multiple waitlists for all schools they have ranked. After August 1, students will remain on only one waitlist for their highest-ranked school, unless a parent contacts a Welcome Center to specify otherwise.
A transfer request will replace any prior assignments, rankings, and previous waitlists. If a transfer is granted, your child will lose their current school year assignment.

If your child is assigned to a high-level-of-need special education program, transfer requests for the 2024-2025 school year will be reviewed in late July/early August of 2024 and then again in November of 2024. For kindergarten programs, requests will also be reviewed in January 2025.

The transfer request policy applies to students moving from one program to the same program at a different school and does not apply to students who need a different school and/or program as determined by the IEP Team.
For more information, please visit the BPS Transferring Schools page: https://www.bostonpublicschools.org/enrollment/welcome-services/transferring-schools
If your child is on a waitlist after a transfer request, they will be considered for placement as seats become available. It's important to stay in contact with the Welcome Center for updates.
After August 1, students will remain on only one waitlist for their highest-ranked school, unless a parent contacts a Welcome Center to specify otherwise.
If a transfer is granted for the current school year, your child will lose their current school year assignment.

Yes, transfer requests for high-level-of-need special education programs will be reviewed in late July/early August of 2024 and then again in November of 2024. For kindergarten programs, requests will also be reviewed in January 2025.
Yes, a transfer request will replace any prior assignments, rankings, and previous waitlists.

Yes, the transfer request policy applies to students moving from one program to the same program at a different school and does not apply to students who need a different school and/or program as determined by the IEP Team.

Registration for students entering K0, K1, K2, Grade 6, Grade 7, and Grade 9 will open on January 6, 2025. Visit bostonpublicschools.org/register for more information and the list of required documents.
Pre-registration is now available online. You can visit bostonpublicschools.org/pre-register to get started and schedule an appointment at bostonpublicschools.org/appointment.
The Dorchester Welcome Center is open Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., and Wednesday from 12 p.m. to 5 p.m. The address is 1216 Dorchester Ave, Dorchester, MA 02125.
Help is available in English, Portuguese, Spanish, Cabo Verdean Creole, and Vietnamese at the Dorchester Welcome Center.

The East Boston Welcome Center is open Monday and Tuesday from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. and Wednesday from 12 p.m. to 5 p.m. (January only). The address is 312 Border Street, Boston, MA 02128. Please note that it is closed on all BPS school holidays.
Help is available in English, Spanish, and Portuguese at the East Boston Welcome Center.
The Roslindale Welcome Center is open Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., and Wednesday from 12 p.m. to 5 p.m. The address is 515 Hyde Park Ave, Boston, MA 02131.
Help is available in Cabo Verdean Creole, English, French, Haitian Creole, Portuguese, and Spanish at the Roslindale Welcome Center.
The Roxbury Welcome Center is open Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., and Wednesday from 12 p.m. to 5 p.m. The address is 2300 Washington Street, Roxbury, MA 02119.

Students registered or who submitted a transfer application for the 2025-2026 school year on or before April 4, 2025, will be on all waitlists for schools ranked higher than their assigned school until August 1, 2025. During this time, students will be assigned to schools from their waitlists as seats become available.

After August 1, 2025, students will automatically remain on only one waitlist—the waitlist for their highest-ranked school—unless a parent contacts a Welcome Center to specify a different school to remain on the waitlist.
Yes, if you are happy with your child's assignment and do not want your child moved into a higher-ranked school, please contact a Welcome Center to remove your child from any waitlists.
You can call or visit a Welcome Center at any time to learn of your child's rank on the waitlist.

Please ensure your phone number and email address are up-to-date in our system. If we do not have accurate contact information, we will not be able to contact your family if a seat opens up, and we will offer the seat to the next student on the waitlist.
Students who register or submit a transfer application for the 2025-2026 school year after April 4, 2025, will automatically be placed on the waitlist for their highest-ranked school.
Waitlists for the 2024-2025 school year expired on November 30, 2024, for grades 1-12 and will expire on January 31, 2025, for grades K0-K2.
Waitlists for the 2025-2026 school year expire on November 30, 2025, for grades 1-12 and January 31, 2026, for grades K0-K2.
A student's position on a waitlist is not guaranteed and is subject to change. Students may move up or down on a waitlist at any time.

For student privacy, BPS is not able to provide specific reasons why a student has moved up or down on a waitlist. However, reasons may include siblings who were not previously linked and students changing educational programs within a school.

Yes, after August 1, 2025, students will automatically remain on only one waitlist for their highest-ranked school, unless a parent contacts a Welcome Center to specify a different school to remain on the waitlist.
Through July 2025, if a seat becomes available, students will be automatically moved into a higher-ranked school off the waitlist.
If you are happy with your child's assignment and do not want your child moved into a higher-ranked school, please contact a Welcome Center to remove your child from any waitlists.
Please ensure your phone number and email address are up-to-date in our system. You can update your contact information by contacting a BPS Welcome Center.
For more information about the BPS waitlist process, please visit: https://www.bostonpublicschools.org/enrollment/welcome-services/wait-lists

BPS uses a Home-Based student assignment policy to assign students to kindergarten through grade 8. It provides a customized list of school choices based on the student’s home address, including schools within a one-mile radius and nearby high-quality schools.

The Home-Based plan offers a list of schools within a one-mile radius of the student’s home. It may also include nearby high-quality schools and additional programmatic offerings. The list may include between 10 and 14 school options.

Parent/Guardians must present a photo ID and two current proofs of Boston residency. Those living under someone else's lease can use the BPS landlord affidavit. Families in homeless shelters may register under the McKinney-Vento Act. Contact a Welcome Center if you're unable to secure acceptable proofs.

Seats are not guaranteed for K0 or K1, as not all schools offer these programs. K0 is especially limited. All K2 students are guaranteed a seat, though not necessarily at a preferred school. Unassigned students may be placed on waitlists.
No. BPS does not offer waivers for the age requirement. Children must be six by September 1 to enter Grade 1.

Families should rank all schools in true order of preference. Changes can be made at a Welcome Center even after assignment, but there’s no guarantee of availability. A photo ID is required for changes.
No. Assignments are made after the close of each registration period based on priorities, random numbers, and school rankings—not the registration date.
Families new to Boston may register at any time at a Welcome Center with the required documents: birth certificate, immunization record, ID, and two proofs of residency.

Inform a Welcome Center immediately. Bring a photo ID and two proofs of the new address. If you're in a new assignment zone, new school choices may be needed unless you handle transportation yourself.

K0–K2 students are assigned only to ranked schools. If no seats are available, they will not be administratively placed, unless a K2 applicant specifically requests it. Older students may be assigned administratively if needed.
Waitlist updates are available about six weeks after registration closes. Parents can call or visit a Welcome Center. Waitlists are created for schools ranked higher than the assigned school.
